narrative.title: Equal-Splitting a Battery Bank
narrative.scenario: A hardware team must arrange m identical cells into a perfect n-sided array where every leg holds the same count - that is, m must be an exact nth power. When the arrangement is impossible, the planner reports failure instead of rounding. Decide whether an integer root exists and return it.
narrative.inputFormat: Two integers n (the root degree) and m (the target value).
narrative.outputFormat: The integer r with r^n == m, or -1 when m has no integer nth root.
constraints: Return -1 rather than a fractional root

testCases.explanation: Three legs of three cells each form the array exactly, since 3 squared is 9.
No integer cubed equals 9, so the arrangement is impossible and -1 is returned.

hintLevels: Level 1: r raised to the n grows monotonically with r, which is exactly the shape a halving search needs.
Level 2: Probe candidate roots between 1 and m and compare the power against m - an exact match returns, otherwise keep the half that could still contain the root.
Level 3: Do not use a floating-point pow helper for the comparison: intermediate rounding betrays exact matches, so accumulate the power with integer multiplication and widen the type.
